story: Fires where a proper name is being completed: the model must supply either the rest of a name whose spelling was cut mid-word or the next capitalised word of a multi-word name.
Fires in the middle of a word that the tokenizer broke apart, predicting the next word-piece that finishes the partially spelled word.
Fires inside a stretch of text that repeats an earlier pattern, copying the separator or word that already followed the same material earlier in the context.
Fires mid-sentence in flowing prose, predicting either the joining punctuation of a compound or the next whole word of the sentence.
Fires at the end of an item in a repeated list or record, predicting the separator that closed the previous items - a comma, a conjunction, or a line break.
Fires where the next token is a repeat of something already present earlier in the context, typically a short punctuation mark, word-piece, or function word.
Fires inside a number or measurement, predicting the punctuation that continues it (the decimal point or time separator after a digit) or the digit that follows.
Fires on the small connector that continues the current item: the hyphen inside a compound, the newline or comma closing an entry, or the next piece of a broken word.
Fires at a clause boundary in prose, predicting the punctuation that ends the clause or the common function word that begins the next one.
Fires when a capitalised name or title is being extended, predicting the next capitalised word or name-piece.
Fires inside a literal string that was already spelled out earlier - a URL, identifier, or bracketed reference - and copies its next piece.
Fires mid-sentence in ordinary prose, predicting the next whole space-prefixed function word such as a determiner or a copula.
Fires where the current phrase needs completing, predicting either the remainder of a split word or the next content word or conjunction of the sentence.
Fires inside a repeated formatted record, reproducing the spacing or punctuation that separated fields the same way earlier in the context.
Fires at the close of a self-contained entry or sentence, predicting the line break or full stop that ends it.
Fires at the end of a descriptive statement, predicting the sentence-final punctuation or the line break that follows it.
Fires deep inside a long prose sentence, predicting the next whole space-prefixed word, whether a conjunction, auxiliary, or content word.
Fires where a syntactic unit has just been completed, predicting either the bracket that closes a parenthetical or the verb that follows the finished subject phrase.
Fires after a preposition or verb that earlier in the same context was followed the same way, predicting the definite article "the".
Fires inside a long or unusual word split across tokens, predicting the suffix word-piece that finishes it rather than copying anything seen earlier.
